lead.t: The resultant “shift to the right” of the oxygen dissociation curve reduces the affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen and results in more complete transfer of oxygen to the tissues.

snip.t: The resultant “shift to the right” of the oxygen dissociation curve reduces the affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen and results in more complete transfer of oxygen to the tissues.
The same shift in the oxygen dissociation curve can also occur at high altitude.

qs.q: A scientist measures the oxygen dissociation curve of hemoglobin and notes a rightward shift in response to increased 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate levels. What is the biochemical basis of this allosteric effect?
o: It binds to the heme iron atoms preventing oxygen molecules from binding.
It increases cooperativity between subunits speeding up total oxygen uptake.
It lowers intracellular pH causing Bohr effect protonation of histidine residues.
It cross-links adjacent beta subunits locking the tetramer in a rigid state.
It stabilizes the deoxy conformation of hemoglobin favoring oxygen release.
qs.e: 2,3-BPG binds in the central cavity of deoxygenated hemoglobin, stabilizing the T state and promoting oxygen unloading.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Biochemistry Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: The 'Oxygen Dissociation Curve' of hemoglobin shifts to the RIGHT in which of the following conditions?
o: Increased PCO2 level in the blood
Increased pH level in the blood
qs.e: A right shift (reduced affinity, easier O2 offloading) is caused by increased H+ (lower pH), increased CO2, increased temperature, and increased 2,3-BPG.
